tldr: On Oct 14 a paper proposed Lifted State Policy Optimization to credit the local change that turns a flawed reasoning state into a better one. ReflectPO (Oct 22) and SOPO (Oct 23) then applied policy optimization to long-horizon agents and hallucination detection.
whats_new: Snyk VulnBench 2.0 (Oct 28) compares deterministic SAST with AI security agents on 108 hand-curated cases, reporting coverage, harness policy and cost, after papers framing the policy as part of the harness.
why_it_matters: The thread shifts from training the policy to the interface around it: the harness and policy together decide agent behavior, so harness changes need their own evals.

beats.headline: Lifted State Policy Optimization targets self-correction
Reflection-guided and multiscale optimization for long-horizon agents
Policy and harness are treated as one system
VulnBench 2.0 measures harness policy and cost against deterministic SAST

open_questions: Do any of these methods publish code or reproducible results on public benchmarks?
Does VulnBench 2.0 get run by anyone outside Snyk's authors?
Do harness-aware evaluations change reported rankings of agents versus bare-model scores?
take_for_builders: Treat these as preprints: before changing a training pipeline, wait for code and replication; meanwhile, rerun your agent evals whenever the harness changes, not only the model.
